metadata.title_zh: DARPA与美国空军成功试飞AI控制F-16
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: DARPA和美国空军成功完成了由人工智能完全控制的F-16战斗机飞行测试，这是自主空战技术从模拟走向现实的关键一步。 此次测试标志着人工智能在复杂、高速的军事航空环境中取得了重大突破，可能彻底改变未来空战模式，加速无人作战平台的部署。 测试飞机配备了特殊接口，允许飞行员通过开关在人类操控和AI操控之间切换，保证了人机协作实验的安全性。AI算法此前已在模拟器中与人类飞行员进行过数千次格斗训练。
metadata.background_zh: DARPA的“空战进化”（ACE）项目旨在通过将人机协作格斗作为挑战问题，建立对作战自主性的信任。该项目从2020年左右开始，AI算法从控制模拟F-16逐步发展到2024年实现真实F-16空中格斗测试，最终达成2026年的全自主飞行。

metadata.title_zh: 付费超过80万美元的基因编辑治疗导致女儿死亡
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 一对夫妇为患有发育障碍的女儿支付超过80万美元接受实验性基因编辑疗法，但该疗法导致女儿死亡，这一悲剧案例此前从未被公开报道。 这起事件凸显了未经充分验证的实验性基因疗法对患者带来的巨大风险，尤其在涉及儿童和脑部治疗时，伦理审查和安全性评估的重要性更为突出。 该疗法使用腺相关病毒（AAV）载体将基因导入大脑，但AAV载体已知具有免疫原性，可能导致严重不良反应。动物实验中也出现了类似副作用，但医生可能低估了风险。
metadata.background_zh: 基因疗法通过载体将正常基因或编辑工具送入细胞，以治疗遗传疾病。AAV是常用的病毒载体之一，但因其可能引发免疫反应而带有黑框警告。将AAV直接注入大脑尤其危险，因为脑部免疫反应难以控制。
metadata.community_discussion_zh: 社区评论普遍批评医生低估风险，尤其质疑选择AAV用于脑部基因治疗。有评论指出，AAV载体的免疫反应风险在已获批疗法中已有记录，而直接注入大脑的风险更大。另一些人认为文章可能夸大事实，但医生表现出的伦理问题仍不可接受。

metadata.title_zh: 创始人吁美勿禁中国开源权重AI
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 多位美国初创公司创始人联名致信特朗普政府，敦促不要禁止中国开源权重AI模型，认为此举将扼杀创新且难以执行。 该事件涉及AI开放与封闭的全球政策博弈，可能影响美国初创企业的技术获取和AI生态的竞争格局。 信中强调，禁止中国开源权重AI模型无助于阻止恶意使用，反而会损害美国初创企业获取先进AI技术的能力，并可能推动中国模型走向更封闭的专有路线。
metadata.background_zh: 开源权重AI模型是指公开训练后的模型权重（即内部参数），允许开发者下载、微调和部署。这类模型通常比完全闭源的商业模型更开放，但权重本身仍可能受版权或协议约束。近年来，中国发布了多个强大的开源权重模型（如Qwen、DeepSeek），引发美国对技术外流和安全的担忧。
metadata.community_discussion_zh: 社区评论普遍质疑禁令的有效性，认为恶意行为者不会遵守法律，且蒸馏（用模型输出训练竞品）在法律上难以被认定侵权。部分评论指出，限制开源权重只会迫使开发者寻找变通路径，最终效果适得其反。

metadata.title_zh: 软件工厂失败原因：仅靠装备工程不够
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 本文指出，当前AI辅助软件开发中的“软件工厂”模式失败，因为过于依赖装备工程（harness engineering），而忽视了更深入的方法，例如针对代码库健康的强化学习（RL）和更好的代码审查（PR review）实践。 这一讨论对软件工程和AI社区意义重大，它揭示了当前AI编码代理策略的局限性，并为未来实现更可维护的代码生成指明了方向——即需要从开发者行为中学习并改善代码审查流程。 文章提到，模型在2025年秋季至2026年春季期间能力大幅提升，因此此前关于代理能力的观点可能已不适用。社区成员还建议创建“可维护性基准”（MaintainabilityBench），奖励检测代码重复、重构或引入新架构层的行为。
metadata.background_zh: 装备工程是一种新兴方法论，侧重于设计系统、工具、约束和反馈循环（即“装备”）来使AI代理可靠工作，而非手动编写代码。然而，本文认为仅靠装备工程不足以维护代码库长期健康，需要结合强化学习（从开发者行为中学习）以及改进的代码审查工具。

metadata.title_zh: 2026年菲尔兹奖揭晓，四位数学家获殊荣
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 2026年菲尔兹奖获奖者公布，授予四位数学家，以表彰他们在调和分析、几何测度论、傅里叶限制、Falconer距离集、Furstenberg集以及Kakeya问题等领域的突破性贡献。 菲尔兹奖是数学界最高荣誉，此次颁奖尤其引人注目：两位华裔数学家自1982年以来首次获奖，同时一位获奖者还共同撰写了关于AI可能带来毁灭性未来的论文，引发广泛讨论。 获奖者的研究工作涉及局部平滑猜想、多尺度与解耦技术、以及三维Kakeya问题；颁奖消息曾因意外提前泄露；此外，其中一位获奖者（Jacob Tsimerman）与Andrew Critch合著了《AI引发的毁灭性未来分类学》论文。
metadata.background_zh: 调和分析是研究函数与信号分解为基本波动的数学分支，核心工具包括傅里叶变换和小波分析；几何测度论则利用测度理论研究欧几里得空间中集合的几何性质，可处理非光滑曲面。这两大领域为上述获奖成果提供了理论基石。

metadata.detailed_summary_zh: Pip 26.2 版本新增了 --only-deps 全局标志，允许用户仅安装项目的依赖项，而无需安装项目本身。该功能通过 PR #13895 实现，解决了长期以来的部署痛点。 这一功能解决了 16 年来 Python 应用部署中的常见 hack，简化了 Docker 镜像构建等场景下的依赖安装流程。它将提升 Python 包管理的一致性和效率，减少临时工作脚本的维护成本。 新标志可与 pip install 配合使用，例如 pip install --only-deps . 会安装 pyproject.toml 中声明的所有依赖，但跳过包本身的安装。该功能支持可选依赖组（如 extras）。
metadata.background_zh: pip 是 Python 的官方包安装器。在依赖管理场景中，用户经常需要先安装依赖（如下载编译依赖）再安装项目本身，传统做法是安装后再卸载，或者使用 requirements.txt 等变通方法。--only-deps 提供了原生支持，消除了这些 hack。

title: Tell HN: Namecheap gave my account to an unverified third party
content:
I’ve been a NameCheap customer for 13 years. I’ve also helped out an old college club paying for a .com they use (that is registered to me under my name, address, and phone number). During a recent leadership transition, the incoming club lead wanted to make changes to the DNS and didn’t know to contact me. They figured out the domain name was parked at NameCheap, so they initiated a password reset using the domain name. I got a password reset email and immediately filed a NameCheap support ticket saying “I did not initiate this”. They called me to verify I was the one who filed the ticket, and then followed up with a canned email with tips like check your anti-virus.

The incoming club leader was persistent though, and called NameCheap support. He convinced them the domain registered in my name and address really belonged to his club, and with no verification or validation whatsoever, NameCheap changed my password, and changed the email address associated with my account. All because someone simply asked nicely on a phone call.

Meanwhile in the background, someone advised the new club leader who I was and we were able to connect and get things transferred over. Ultimately I was happy to give them access or even ownership if they wanted (student club turnover being what it is, it’s likely a domain doesn’t get renewed and gets gobbled up by a squatter, which is why I was keeping it current for them).

But NameCheap had no way of knowing any of this. As far as NameCheap was aware, this was a personal account of mine. They demonstrated they were perfectly able to pick up a phone and call me (to verify my initial support ticket) but when someone calls them and says “but I really want access to that account” they don’t bother?

I’d hesitate to even call this social engineering. It’s clearly a massive vulnerability. I’ve already moved a dozen of my most critical domains out of NameCheap after seeing just how easy it is for a third party to completely take over a NameCheap account: just ask nicely. --- Top Comments --- [petecooper]: +1 for Porkbun. I use tld-list.com to shop around for registrars when I need a TLD that Porkbun don't handle. [pilingual]: Namecheap has been owned by a private equity firm for several months now. It would be nice to have a nonprofit registrar so jumping every few years isn't necessary. [Adachi91]: I moved from Namecheap 2 years ago when I had auto renew on but it did not auto-renew, which their system automatically turns your domain into an advertisement hell page. Transfer system was locked and I contacted them and told them to transfer it to my other registrar or I would file an ICANN complaint. I moved it to my main registrar (Hover) which while more expensive I haven't a problem with them in the decades I've been with them. My original registrar shutdown sometime in the m... [geuis]: I've been a long, long term customer of Namecheap as well. Domain privacy protection is a feature that Namecheap provides for all valid domains. Its included by default at no extra cost. The poster didn't indicate if they had this feature enabled or not for the domain. It would have prevented the college club person from even seeing their email address to initiate a password reset. This clearly isn't an answer for NC's customer support personnel and company policies. But I... [ryandrake]: This kind of story makes me wonder what's the most popular/valuable domain I can take control of simply by being convincing over the phone. Sounds tempting! I can't even log in to most web sites anymore without doing a side-trip to my E-mail inbox, "for enhanced security," but these clowns let you just take a domain by asking nicely! --- From hackernews --- I’ve been building Echo (https://echo.tracerml.ai/), an experiment in making one AI system out of a pool of open-weight models rather than choosing a single model and using it for every task.

It started with a simple experiment. I took a group of models, including GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7 and others, and ran them on the same evaluations. Then I measured what would happen if, for each problem, you somehow knew in advance which models would be useful and how their outputs should be combined.

That hypothetical system performed substantially better than any individual model in the pool. Of course, it is not something you can actually deploy because it relies on knowing which decisions were good after seeing the result. Echo is my attempt to recover some of that advantage without having that information in advance.

For each request, Echo decides how much computation to allocate, which models should participate, and how their work should be combined. Some prompts may only need a relatively small amount of inference, while others benefit from multiple models working on different parts of the problem.

One thing that surprised me while building it was how complementary the models are. A model that is clearly weaker overall can still be extremely useful on particular problems or as part of a combination.

On my first evaluation mix, Echo consistently performed better than the best individual model in its pool. It also reached roughly the same aggregate result as Fable, which I used as one of the stronger comparison systems, at around one third of the inference cost.

There are still some cases where Echo makes the wrong allocation or combination decision. I’m currently spending a lot of time understanding those failures, as well as testing whether the same approach holds up on coding and agentic tasks where measuring the quality of each decision becomes much harder.

I built a chat interface (echo.tracerml.ai) and an OpenAI-compatible API (https://echo.tracerml.ai/docs/api) so the system can be tested outside the evaluation setup.

Here is a short/high level video on how it works: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJFJSvOdXhg

I wrote up the evaluation methodology, individual model results, costs and current limitations here: https://echo.tracerml.ai/eval

I would love for you to try it! Especially if you hit any weird failure cases or places where the allocation looks unintuitive. --- Top Comments --- [qainsights]: Can't sign up: `too many authentication attempts` [dluan]: So this is the dogpile.com of the askjeeves, alta vista, and lycos approach? Time is a flat circle? [cheema33]: > Fable-level results at 1/3 the cost I am guessing this is not targeting those of us on the heavily subsidized $200/mo plans. Sure, these plans may be temporary, but none of us really know how temporary they are. Until then, 1/3rd of the published API pricing is not very appealing. [islambaraka]: What signals does Echo use to decide which models should participate before it has seen their outputs? [raver1975]: I can't sign up: too many authentication attempts

metadata.title_zh: Namecheap安全漏洞：客服未经验证移交账户
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 一名用户报告称，Namecheap客服在未进行任何身份验证的情况下，仅凭一个第三方电话请求就更改了其账户密码和关联邮箱，导致账户被完全接管。 此事件暴露了域名注册商在账户恢复流程中的严重安全漏洞，可能被社交工程攻击利用，导致用户域名被劫持或数据泄露，影响所有Namecheap用户的信任。 受害者已提交工单并接到客服回电确认身份，但后续客服仍接受了第三方的声称，直接修改了账户凭证；Namecheap未使用双因素认证或额外验证步骤。
metadata.background_zh: 域名注册商是管理域名注册和DNS设置的服务商，账户安全性至关重要。社交工程是一种通过心理操纵获取信息或系统访问权限的攻击方式，常见于电话诈骗（vishing）。域名劫持可能导致网站无法访问、数据泄露或恶意重定向。
metadata.community_discussion_zh: 社区用户对Namecheap的安全措施表示强烈批评，并推荐Porkbun、Hover等替代注册商；有用户指出Namecheap已被私募股权收购后服务质量下降；也有人建议启用域名隐私保护（WHOIS隐私）来防止公开暴露注册信息。

title: What happened to TheNumbers.com
content:

[primitivesuave]: A couple years ago, I was running a website which allowed the public to view all the US government handouts to small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic. It also tracked all the fraudulent loans being prosecuted by the DOJ, and allowed anyone to run structured queries over the public dataset. There was a "donate" button which took in ~$2k in donations over the lifetime of the site, and you could download the entire underlying dataset (around 10 GB uncompressed) for free directly...

That, coupled with a bot-aware CDN should keep them online at a reasonable cost for many years to come. Otherwise, I'm very curious to know more about their old and new architecture and what sorts of mitigation/scaling strategies they've started using to keep the s...

[abetusk]: I think people are missing one of the points of the article. It's not just that agents are hammering the site, it's that there might be lurking vulnerabilities that allow malicious usage, which is why it went down, then came back up with a fraction of the data and a reduced design. The article says (speculates?) that malicious users are trying to get privileged access for an edge in prediction market betting. From the article: > If you could see The Numbers data before everyone e...

[podgietaru]: "One Reddit theory even suggested it was a deliberate rug pull designed to cripple the free site to push people towards paid products." I know this isn't really the point of the article, but I've been thinking about this a lot. I wonder if we're going to see more resources go this way. I used to publish little doo-dads as opensource software. Not because it was something that was legitimately ground breaking or anything (it absolutely wasn't) but because I had a ...

[gajus]: What a throwback. Back in 2015 I have started Applaudience, which at the time was the only provider of real-time cinema ticket sales data. I still remember comparing our numbers against TheNumbers.com as part of calibration. I have since moved on to other businesses, but this remains one of my favorite pieces of technology that I have developed. Would love to bring it back one day.

metadata.title_zh: TheNumbers.com 遭恶意爬虫攻击被迫精简

metadata.title_zh: ATProto应用构建：公共数据与权限需求的矛盾
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: 一篇博客文章和Hacker News讨论指出，在AT协议上构建应用时，其所有数据默认公开的设计与需要私密或权限数据的场景存在根本矛盾。 这揭示了去中心化社交协议设计中的核心权衡，可能影响开发者选择平台以及ATProto生态的未来发展方向。 Luke Kanies在文章中批评当前权限数据提案将访问控制编码到记录URI中，认为这破坏了设计一致性；社区成员pfraze回应称团队正在收集反馈。
metadata.background_zh: AT Protocol（ATProto）是Bluesky社交网络的基础协议，采用联邦架构，所有数据默认公开存储于个人数据服务器（PDS）上，任何应用都可读取。这种设计旨在实现数据可移植性和互操作性，但难以支持需要细粒度权限的应用场景。
metadata.community_discussion_zh: 评论者ekosz认为许多应用试图将方形钉子（私有数据需求）放入圆孔（ATProto公开设计），并指出如果数据默认加密会破坏协议核心优势。另有人分享了在ATProto上构建桌游社区的成功体验，也有用户质疑是否应改用ActivityPub。

title: Show HN: Palmier Pro – Open-source macOS video editor built for AI
content:
Hi HN, we are Marcos and Harrison, cofounders of Palmier (https://palmier.io). We are building Palmier Pro, an open source macOS video editor, with built-in AI generation and a local MCP server that connects to your agent. Here are a few demos:

- Making some AI transitions: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hbM_-eR1GX4

- Multicam editing with Codex: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SjS2q2LT1q8

- Cutting long form clips into shorts: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PR66eN2ouuQ

We built Palmier Pro as an internal tool when we were making AI launch videos for other startups. The main problem it solved in the beginning was the back-and-forth between AI generation platform and video editor. The iteration loop was awkward: AI videos → download → import to editor → edit → realize we need to change the AI video → repeat. So we built a minimal video editor where we could let Claude generate AI videos inside the editor.

As we gave more and more tools to the agent, we wanted to push to see what else agents can do in the video editing space. So today, your Claude/Codex can:

- Manage projects inside Palmier Pro

- Import media from a public URL or filesystem to the project, and organize them in folders

- Search media (by embedding footages using SigLIP2 running locally)

- Edit the timeline (tracks/clips/keyframes operations)

- Generate images, videos, sound effects, captions, music

- Export videos

There are two ways for LLMs to interact with the editor: by connecting to the local MCP server, or using the in-app chat. Both use the same tools and APIs exposed by the video editor.

We have seen people using MCP server to connect to their own workflow to automate massive-scale video editing (e.g. given this same podcast style, replicate it with other footages that I have). We have also seen people using the in-app chat where it lives closer to the editor UI, with lower latency for faster iteration.

We don't believe that AI is going to replace human creativity (nor should it), but where it can really help is in automating the gruntwork in video editing. Most work in the editing workflow is more mechanical than creative. Our vision is to build a video editor where AI can enable more individuals to create.

Throughout our experiments, AI is not very good at creative editing, but given a pattern (transcription-based, beat-based), it can do a decent job at rough cut.

We built Palmier Pro in Swift as an MVP because we wanted better performance and minimal dependencies (no nodejs/webview), with some native macOS APIs like SpeechAnalyzer and CoreML for us to run some models locally. We use SpeechAnalyzer for local transcriber, SigLip2 to embed video frames, beat_this for beat detection, Silero VAD for silence detection, all running locally. The tradeoff is that we don't support Linux or Windows at the moment.

Palmier Pro is open source and free to try out (macOS 26 only at the moment, though - we'll support more platforms over time, but for now are focusing on iterating the core product).

No login required except for the AI generation features, which route requests to our backend. We are offering free credits on sign up so you can try out the AI generation as well.

We'd love to hear your feedback! --- Top Comments --- [Marciplan]: This looks great! Have you thought about dropping the 'subscription'-part and 'just' selling credits instead? Here's my thinking as a SaaS founder: when I launch a product, I don't need a video every month. So a monthly pricing makes me do this little calculation every time: "do I need a video this month? nah. Then I'll wait. I lose the early-bird price, but I still net out cheaper." And since there's no yearly option, there's nothing pul... [nsbk]: This is what I have been waiting for in order to process my massive action camera library, I will definitely give it a try! I will start with older standard GoPro videos, and hope that by the time I make it to the Insta360 videos the editor supports 360 video (unless it does already!) [misterchocolat]: I've been following Marcos's youtube channel and it's so great to see that they've finally found their thing. Looks like an awesome product that people actually want. Well done. [mrkstu]: I assume using Swift means cross-platform support is tertiary at best? I have mostly Macs in my workflow so not an issue for me, but its good to have that plainly stated if so. Being able to edit a long video to pull out different speakers segments automatically or do automatic edits of speaker transitions would be great- I'll give it a try and see what scenarios are best suited for our use cases... [didriksg]: Seems super convenient! I spent yesterday trying to edit a simple video for a project by hand and it was not a fun experience! Will check it out!

title: The PImpl idiom and the C++26 std::indirect type
content: Comments
author: mariusbancila.ro via raymii

metadata.title_zh: C++26 std::indirect 简化 PImpl 惯用法
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: C++26 引入了 std::indirect 类型，这是一种拥有值语义的堆分配包装器，可用于更简洁地实现 PImpl 惯用法。 传统 PImpl 实现依赖指针（如 std::unique_ptr），存在复制语义和 const 传播问题。std::indirect 提供了真正的值语义，能够正确管理对象生命周期并避免手动编写特殊成员函数，对大型 C++ 项目的封装和编译防火墙有重要意义。 std::indirect 对象在移动后变为无值（valueless）状态，其复制操作会深拷贝堆上对象，从而保证值语义的正确性。编译器会根据 std::indirect 自动生成正确的默认成员函数，减少样板代码。
metadata.background_zh: PImpl（Pointer to Implementation）是 C++ 中常用的设计模式，将类的实现细节隐藏在私有指针后，以减少编译依赖。传统上常使用 std::unique_ptr 或原始指针实现，但需要手动编写复制和移动操作，且 const 传播不完美。std::indirect 是 C++26 标准库新增的类模板，它封装堆分配的对象并提供值语义，可自动处理复制、移动和析构。

metadata.title_zh: Brendan Gregg 展示用 eBPF 追踪 TCP 连接生命周期
metadata.detailed_summary_zh: Brendan Gregg 于 2016 年发布博客，介绍了基于 eBPF 和 BCC 的新工具 tcplife，该工具能够追踪 TCP 会话的打开和关闭事件，并输出每个会话的生命周期时长等详细信息。 tcplife 让系统管理员和性能工程师无需修改内核代码即可动态追踪 TCP 连接生命周期，有助于诊断网络性能问题和优化服务，展示了 eBPF 在 Linux 网络监控中的实际价值。 tcplife 通过内核动态追踪（kprobes）和 eBPF 实现，可捕获 TCP 连接的建立与关闭，输出 PID、端口、数据量、时长等信息，支持按 PID 或端口过滤，并能显示时间戳和吞吐量统计。
metadata.background_zh: eBPF（扩展伯克利包过滤器）是 Linux 内核的一项技术，允许安全高效地运行用户定义的程序；BCC 是基于 eBPF 的工具集，方便创建追踪程序。tcplife 是 BCC 工具之一，专门用于追踪 TCP 会话生命周期。
